project.name: Rushden Historic Town Explorer

properties.name: Rushden curated visitor boundary
properties.methodology: Morphological closing of the preserved official built-up-area geometry using a 300 metre outward and inward buffer. This fills internal omissions for connected parks, river corridors and visitor green spaces without applying a general outward town buffer.

project.boundarySource: Curated Rushden visitor boundary derived from ONS Built-up Areas (December 2024)
project.researchNotes:
Townscape Guides audit completed 2026-08-09. The unchanged ONS 2024 built-up area is the active inclusion boundary. Historic England designations and public current OpenStreetMap visitor facilities were filtered point-in-polygon. Historic England official list-entry date enrichment completed 2026-08-09: 9 of 20 statutory records now carry defensible date evidence; unresolved entries were individually checked and retained as unknown.

Broad visitor-attraction editorial discovery pass 2026-08-13: expanded See discovery beyond historic records using a local OSM extract. Automatically discovered additions remain below Recommended until source-backed editorial review.

touristAppeal.label: Local detour
touristAppeal.summary: Two volunteer museums, a handsome parish church and Hall Park create a credible local-history visit, though Rushden remains a modest visitor stop.

townGuide.headline: Boot-and-shoe stories, transport history and a generous town park
townGuide.intro: Rushden’s visitor interest comes from its industrial and transport collections. Link the station museum and town museum with St Mary’s and Rushden Hall Park.
perfectFor: A rewarding specialist detour when the museums are open, rather than a broad tourist destination.

suggestedFirstVisit.summary: Check the volunteer museum openings first, then link the former station with Rushden Museum, St Mary’s and Hall Park.
